NARRATOR.desc: Documentary narrator: confident, brisk, dry wit, suspense on the reveals

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 1971, a man in a business suit hijacked a plane with nothing but a briefcase and a note.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He demanded $200,000 and four parachutes. And he got them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Most of the passengers never even knew they had been hijacked.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then, over the dark forests of Washington, he lowered the rear stairs of a Boeing 727, and jumped into the night.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The FBI hunted him for forty-five years. Spy planes. Soldiers in the woods. More than 800 suspects.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 1980, an eight-year-old boy dug up some of the money, rotting in the sand by a river.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But the man himself? Never found. Not a body. Not even his name.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Because even D.B. Cooper was a reporter's mistake.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So who was he, and did he survive? The full story is on Ink and Antiquity.
